artifacts.synopsis: TEs Felipe Assis and Carter Brown appealed South Florida Presbytery's decision to divest them without censure after their churches left the PCA. The SJC sustained the consolidated appeals, held that BCO 13-2 and 34-10 did not authorize divestiture on these facts, reversed the action, restored both ministers to good standing, and directed constitutionally appropriate further action.

artifacts.synopsis: Arizona Presbytery divested a minister without censure for prolonged lack of call after he had joined an EPCEW congregation and notified Presbytery of his withdrawal. The SJC sustained his appeal and reversed the divestiture because BCO 38-3(a) had already ended Presbytery's jurisdiction while he was in good standing and under no investigation or charges. It directed Presbytery to record the irregular withdrawal, acknowledge his new membership, and remove him from its roll.

artifacts.synopsis: A member removed from the rolls under BCO 38-4 challenged Presbytery's ruling that she lacked standing to complain because she was no longer a member. The SJC sustained the complaint: standing under BCO 43-1 cannot be defeated by the very removal challenged. Removal under BCO 38-4 is pastoral discipline, a disciplinary case, not a merely administrative act. The SJC remanded to Presbytery to consider the complaint and take the action it should have taken—remand to the Session. The merits of the removal were not decided.

artifacts.title: Presbytery's investigative duty when a new body holds evangelical beliefs

matches.evidence: The CCB advised that a presbytery's BCO 2-2 inquiry ends once it concludes a newly formed entity holds a fairly traditional evangelical set of beliefs.
